overview: The Medford Human Rights Commission approved a statement for International Human Rights Day and finalized plans for a February reading of Belinda’s Petition at the Royall House. The meeting also included coordination for Martin Luther King Jr. Day service events and a discussion regarding the commission's policy for issuing statements on global incidents.

items.title: Introductions and Meeting Touchstones
items.summary: Commissioners and staff introduced themselves and read the commission's guiding touchstones aloud.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the meeting minutes from October.

items.title: International Human Rights Day Statement
items.summary: Approved a draft statement for International Human Rights Day pending a minor typographical correction and discussed distributing it to the City Council and Senior Center.

items.title: Black History Month Planning
items.summary: Decided to proceed with a second annual public reading of Belinda’s Petition at the Royall House and Slave Quarters in February.

items.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Day Service Planning
items.summary: Proposed designating January as a month of service and requested commissioners gather a list of local volunteer opportunities by the end of November.

items.title: Lunar New Year Collaboration
items.summary: Discussed partnering with the public library and local Asian-American cultural organizations for family-friendly events in February.

items.title: Police Department Community Engagement
items.summary: Chief Jack Buckley provided an update on monthly police service events, including coat drives, food drives, and blood drives.

items.title: ICCM Window Maintenance Clarification
items.summary: Director Nwajei reported that tarped windows at the Islamic Cultural Center of Medford were the result of scheduled remodeling rather than vandalism.

items.title: Massachusetts Human Rights Coalition
items.summary: Announced that Medford is a founding member of the coalition and invited commissioners to join the organization's communication group.

items.title: Charter Study Commission Updates
items.summary: Provided a schedule for upcoming listening sessions and encouraged the community to complete the city charter review survey by December 1.

items.title: Mobile Vaccine Clinic Announcement
items.summary: Announced a COVID-19 and flu vaccine clinic at City Hall scheduled for November 17.

items.title: Policy for Statements of Sentiment
items.summary: Responded to a resident request regarding the Nepal earthquake by approving a motion to include a formal discussion on the policy of issuing 'statements of sentiment' on the December agenda.
